significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that a measurable aggregate signature—defined through “digit/leading-digit frequencies, value distribution, n-gram/positional patterns, entropy”—predicts transmission strength beyond divergence-token frequency, and that erasing this signature causally suppresses transmission. This combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) causal claim, constraining which datasets should transmit traits and supporting both a behavioral phenomenon and a data-side carrier mechanism, though not a model-internal mechanism. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure of decoding, independent prediction, and targeted suppression would rule out this aggregate-statistical account within the stated feature class and favor rare-token or other accounts, although it would not prove them uniquely; Cloud et al.’s matched-base result and the divergence-token account in “Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning” make carrier identity a consequential explanatory question. In the topic-substitution check, merely restating “extend subliminal learning” would not justify this score; the above-median value comes specifically from the claimed coupling and targeted causal erasure rather than the topic’s general importance.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the “trait-agnostic Distribution-Matching Resampling defense,” accompanied by a statistical-signature audit; it is ex ante because it operates “at the data-ingestion stage” before student training or deployment, giving distillation consumers an action window without teacher-model access. After recalibration against a control distribution, the claim predicts a transferable qualitative relation—larger signature implies stronger transmission and matching it away suppresses transmission—rather than merely supplying a procedure to rediscover an arbitrary direction, although its asserted scope is strongest for synthetic number data and only secondarily extends to code carriers. The downstream users include practitioners who audit, gate, or ingest synthetic training data, not only subliminal-learning researchers; the topic-substitution check fails to preserve this score because the generic topic supplies neither this model-free screen nor the pre-training intervention.
